title: APIs as resource servers
subtitle: Stateless JWT validation for /api/** in every service
summary: Every service exposes /api/v1 through a second, stateless filter chain that validates bearer JWTs from Keycloak: signature against the realm's JWKS, issuer, expiry and the turfclub-api audience. The principal is preferred_username, so audit trails show service-account-svc-racing or a person's username.

sections.title: API filter chain (order 1)
JWT converter
A write endpoint guarded per method
Design points
items: Two SecurityFilterChain beans: @Order(1) matches /api/** (stateless, no CSRF, bearer tokens); @Order(2) is the session-based UI.
audiences: turfclub-api in application.yml rejects tokens minted for other purposes.
Errors come back as JSON (ApiExceptionHandler), never as an HTML login page.
The core audit API adds a class-level @PreAuthorize("@auditApi.canRead(authentication)"): TC_AUDITOR, TC_ADMIN or the listed chatbot client only.

episode.title: One service, two filter chains: UI sessions and API tokens
episode.hook: Same Spring Boot app, two completely different security models. Here is how they coexist.
objectives: Configure a resource server with audience validation
